channel.title: Foremerge blog
channel.description: Coordinating parallel coding agents, above Git.

item.title: Coding agents stop mid-task. Our coordination store had 3,896 stale conflicts
item.description: Agent sessions end without closing their work, and a coordination store that treats abandoned plans as live fills up with noise. What Foremerge 0.6.0 changes, and why.

item.title: What is an intent conflict?
item.description: An intent conflict is two declared plans that cannot both be true. Git cannot see one, because it compares lines, not plans. A definition, an example and what it is not.

item.title: Worktrees do not remove the collision. They move it to merge time.
item.description: Git worktrees stop agents overwriting each other's files. The collision between their plans is still there, and you find it at merge time. Here is a run you can repeat.

item.title: Running multiple Claude Code agents in parallel: what worktrees cannot see
item.description: Give each agent its own worktree, split the work by what each task changes, and test the merged result. That handles files. It does not handle two plans that cannot both be true, and Git will merge those without a word.

item.title: AI agents introduced several new layers to the development stack. You are probably missing this one.
item.description: The stack grew five layers in two years, and each was adopted fast because its absence hurt the same day. The sixth one's absence hurts three days later. That is the only reason you are probably missing it.

item.title: Agent orchestrators and agent coordinators are not the same layer
item.description: Both words mean make several agents work together, so they get used interchangeably. They name different layers, and one question tells you which one you are running.

item.title: 31 hard questions about coordinating parallel coding agents, answered
item.description: A reader went through the Foremerge source and asked 31 questions about design, trust, and roadmap. The full maintainer Q&A, lightly edited.

item.title: Parallel coding agents without the carnage
item.description: Two agents, two worktrees, zero textual conflict, and a clean merge that broke anyway. Worktrees isolate files, not plans, and Git compares diffs, not intentions.
